# Mutation sweep: does the suite still catch each fix's defect at HEAD?
# Method: worktree at HEAD, revert the fix (or apply mutations/<finding>.patch),
# run the module, compare against the all-green CONTROL run. Every row MEASURED,
# nothing predicted.
# "Baseline" is NOT this. In this project it means the pre-verification RTL;
# see formal/tools/baseline/MANIFEST.tsv, a different measurement with a different
# question. Nothing in this file uses the word.
# class   rtl | harness   WHAT is being mutated.
#         Most rows mutate the DESIGN and ask whether the instrument still sees
#         the defect. A harness row mutates the INSTRUMENT and asks whether it
#         is load-bearing at all; the column exists to keep that distinction
#         visible rather than to sort the file.
# head    the HEAD each row's outcome was MEASURED at.
#         The sweep runs at current HEAD by design: "does the suite still catch
#         this" is a question about the code as it stands, not a historical
#         replay. So as HEAD moves past a row's recorded one the driver WARNS but
#         still runs, and a changed outcome is then a real result rather than
#         drift. Use `regress.sh --replay ...` to rebuild a row at the HEAD it
#         was recorded at, which is what makes the numbers below reproducible
#         rather than merely dated.
# method  revert | patch
# expect  cex:<leaf>            named property must be in the counterexample list
#         cover-unreachable     one or more covers must come back UNREACHABLE (vacuity)
#         elab-fail             the run must stop at the elaboration gate
#                               ("ELABORATION FAILED:") with NO property table.
#                               harness-gate is the same class at the
#                               multiple-driver gate.
#         harness-gate          run aborts on the multiple-driver check, no property table
#         timeout               proof stops converging (weakest: names no property)
#         none                  NOTHING detects it; see notes. A `none` row is not a
#                               non-result: it pins a measured green, so a future change
#                               that starts detecting it reports *** CHANGED ***. Rows
#                               with this expectation are the tripwire on a retraction:
#                               the only thing that would notice if a future change
#                               started detecting a defect the record says is not there.
# THE DRIVER CHECKS THE expect FIELD ONLY, and that is deliberate. The proven/cex
# counts in the notes are prose and are not parsed, so a row can drift in its
# counts and still report CAUGHT. This file is a way to REPRODUCE an issue, not a
# golden transcript of a run: what a row promises is that the named detector
# still fires, and pinning the surrounding counts would fail the sweep on
# unrelated proof progress. Read the counts as context for what you should
# expect to see, not as an assertion.
#finding

TIMEOUT at 600s. NOT a sizing artifact: identical config, and the control run's slowest property proves in 174s (roughly 3.5x headroom at the 600s ceiling). That headroom is the reason the ceiling must not go lower: below ~2x, 'did not converge' stops being distinguishable from 'slow'. CI goes red but no property is named.

GREEN 20/0, mutation verified real (3 guards removed). Guards KEPT. Not a formal-only blind spot: the sim half is also blind, and was measured. At QUEUE_SIZE=15, instrumented identically, the deepest level is entered 1452 times in BOTH builds and X reaches the comparator inputs 0 times guarded / 2159 times unguarded: reachable, heavily exercised, genuinely injecting X, and the suite is green anyway because X never reaches o_data and every check watches the port. The RTL settles why: an explicit `parent_lvl == TREE_DEPTH-1` override at the end of the same combinational arm zeroes next_parent_lvl/next_parent_idx and forces both write enables low, so nothing tainted is ever committed. The walk terminates BY DESIGN, not by accident. Synthesis agrees where there is no X at all: out-of-context synthesis gives near-identical LUT/FF/CARRY8/RAM utilization guarded vs unguarded, with the guarded build using slightly more decode logic for identical state, which points away from a write-aliasing hazard. Not a proven equivalence: different netlists, no formal equivalence check. Two level_1[parent_idx] sites are in range only by an invariant the walk maintains, not by construction: a_level1_index_in_range in hwpq_bram_aux.sv asserts it and PROVES; c_deepest_level_walked separately shows the deepest level is reached, so the guards are a decision about reachable cycles rather than a hypothetical.

GREEN 20/0, guard verified removed. NOT a hole: a_no_placeholder_at_capacity PROVES, so the overflow state cannot occur. With a sound RAM model, a_occ_bounded and a_queue_size_bounded both PROVE while c_root_placeholder_nonempty still covers.

GREEN 20 proven/0 cex/35 covers, byte-identical to unmodified HEAD. NOTHING detects it. Not merely unexercised: the precondition is REACHABLE (c_walk_runs_during_fill and c_walk_dirties_fill both cover in 2 cycles on the reverted design); the corruption simply does not survive to $fell(filling) at QUEUE_SIZE=7, DATA_WIDTH=2.

THE ONLY HARNESS-CLASS ROW. 9 asserts proven and 0 cex, IDENTICAL to a clean run, beside c_reset_reasserted UNREACHABLE. The whole finding is the one cover. Mutates the INSTRUMENT, not the design: it is the only row that tests whether the harness is load-bearing. Revert is wrong: the fixing commit rewrites eleven other proof configs and adds a new spec file; the patch restores the pre-harness elaborate/reset pair on ONE module.
